newsitem.title: CHINA: Zhengzhou adds one hour to boost wheat trading.
newsitem.headline: Zhengzhou adds one hour to boost wheat trading.

text.p: China's Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange has launched a special one-hour session for trading of wheat futures to try to revive interest in the commodity, exchange officials said on Monday.

From October 3, the exchange set aside one hour each afternoon when only wheat futures could be traded, he said. That would encourage traders to focus on wheat futures and boost their transactions, one exchange official said.
"The special trading hour was designed to stimulate wheat futures," he said. Trading of wheat futures has been sluggish recently because of high activity in green bean futures, he said.
Trading volume and price fluctuations of wheat futures on the exchange had increased since the start of the special trading session, the Futures Herald newspaper said.
China's securities authorities have been encouraging futures exchanges to revive trading of some stable commodities to provide hedging opportunities.
